raw_request: Preserve current behavior while redesigning ZTerm client and daemon ownership, separating data/control/debug/error planes, adding debuggable foundation nodes, and pluginizing the client with a Cordis-compatible host boundary.
understood_objective: Deliver ZTERM-ARCH-V2-DESIGN-001 through AppSDK-governed slices so client and daemon modules have unique physical ownership, typed adjacent message chains, independent debug/control centers, debuggable foundation nodes, and capability-scoped client plugins without changing product or business payload semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Client and daemon production source has exact module ownership and an acyclic registered dependency graph.
Data, control, debug, and error planes use physically separate typed contracts and channels.
Foundation nodes expose deterministic lifecycle, bounded debug subscription, and versioned immutable snapshots.
Buffer frame assembly, sparse buffer, render window, DOM renderer, UI shell, connection, terminal channel, input, daemon mirror, and daemon input queue are independent owners.
Client features consume declared capabilities through one plugin host; Cordis, if selected, is isolated behind an adapter and excluded from hot paths.
SessionContext, server composition, and message routing no longer own cross-domain business state.
Current terminal, session, input, file, schedule, and remote-window behavior and business payload semantics remain unchanged.
Every implementation slice passes AppSDK evidence, review, compile, promotion, Active, Protected, regression, and freeze gates.
non_goals: No fallback, dual production route, dual compiler, or second SDK.
No Mac, Windows, or wterm runtime refactor.
No Cordis/global event bus in terminal frame, mirror, buffer, renderer, transport, input, file-chunk, or media-frame hot paths.
assumptions: The AppSDK project root remains android because it contains the current Android client and embedded daemon mainline.
packages/shared changes are limited to registered typed contracts required by Android client/daemon edges.
Target-state modules remain design or pending until owned paths, source bindings, and required gates exist.
